identity.title: SEDEBLEND: a new method for deblending spectral energy distributions in confused imaging
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: we adapt the forward-modelling method that we originally developed to disentangle a high-redshift strongly-lensed galaxy group, in order to tackle this problem in a more statistically rigorous way

targets.name: ALESS (ALMA follow-up of LESS) submm galaxies in ECDFS

evidence.quote: We apply our method to the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) Survey of Submillimetre Galaxies (cite: alma) in the Extended Chandra Deep Field South (ECDFS)
We apply our method to the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) Survey of Submillimetre Galaxies (cite: alma) in the Extended Chandra Deep Field South (ECDFS)

question.value: Can source deblending and SED fitting be combined in one forward-modelling MCMC to derive far-IR luminosities and dust temperatures of ALESS submm galaxies from confused Herschel imaging plus ALMA fluxes?

evidence.quote: by combining source deblending and SED fitting into the same procedure. We call this method “SEDeblend.”
The ALMA observations were carried out under program 2011.0.00294.S.

bands.value: Band 7 (345 GHz, 870 um); Band 9 only simulated

evidence.quote: The data used in this study are at 345 GHz in ALMA Band 7
Fig. [1](#subtraction) shows the ECDFS field at the three *Herschel*-SPIRE wavelengths
Because the 160 $\mu$m PACS data are dominated by instrumental noise
the catalogue of nearby Multiband Imaging Photometer for Spitzer (MIPS) 24 $\mu$m and Very Large Array (VLA) sources provided in (cite: swinbank)
we use the ALMA 870 $\mu$m fluxes and positions from (cite: alma)

what.value: photometric redshifts used as Gaussian priors

evidence.quote: The photometric redshift constraints are considered to be $\pm1\,\sigma$ Gaussian priors in our model.

what.value: NMJS catalogue of 24um and VLA sources

evidence.quote: henceforth referred to as the NMJS catalogue

what.value: Symeonidis sample catalogue of luminosities and dust temperatures

evidence.quote: We obtained the catalogue of sources used to create the estimate of the $L$–$T_\mathrm{d}$ relation of (cite: symeonidis)
Calibration uncertainties are 10% and 20% in Bands 7 and 9, respectively.

what.value: Forward-modelling MCMC method and modified blackbody SED with power-law

evidence.quote: We adopt a modified blackbody SED with a power-law component for the shorter wavelengths, as in M14.

what.value: Duplicate NMJS source rejection within 1.5 arcsec

evidence.quote: As in (cite: swinbank), we treat any source in the NMJS catalogue as a duplicate if it is within 1.5 arcseconds of an ALESS source or another NMJS source.

unstated_but_needed: MCMC chain length, convergence criteria and proposal settings
Priors on luminosity normalisation and background
Exact SED model parameterisation (power-law component details)
Region sizes used for likelihood radius
Details of SPIRE/PACS map versions and pixel preparation

method.value: Maximum-likelihood fit of model SEDs to all NMJS and ALESS sources, equal pixel weights, then subtract

evidence.quote: we use the ECDFS SPIRE residuals, after subtracting our model SED, fit to every NMJS and ALESS source simultaneously.

key_parameters.value: Region with 250 um instrumental noise < 1.2 mJy, 4024 sources

evidence.quote: We limit this process to the region where the 250 $\mu$m instrumental noise is less than 1.2 mJy, which includes 4024 sources

validation.value: Stacking on real and model sky gave consistent results

evidence.quote: Because the stacking on the real and model sky give consistent results, we conclude that we are not significantly over-subtracting flux density from our maps.

method.value: Inverse covariance from random 10x10 pixel cutouts of residuals; median per angular separation, polynomial for cross-band

evidence.quote: We can estimate the covariance for an image of $10\times10$ pixels at each of the three SPIRE channels by selecting randomly chosen cutouts from the residuals

method.value: MCMC Metropolis-Hastings with Gibbs sampling, SPIRE correlated likelihood, PACS and ALMA Gaussian likelihoods

evidence.quote: the model is fit to the data using an MCMC Metropolis-Hastings algorithm (cite: mcmc1; mcmc2) with Gibbs sampling (cite: gibbs).

key_parameters.value: beta fixed at 1.5; Td hard prior 10-100 K; LFIR integrated 8-1000 um

evidence.quote: we simply fix it to a nominal value of 1.5
Far-IR luminosities are calculated by integrating the model SED from 8 to 1000 $\mu$m.

assumptions.value: Photometric redshift as +/-1 sigma Gaussian priors; Planck cosmology

evidence.quote: The photometric redshift constraints are considered to be $\pm1\,\sigma$ Gaussian priors in our model.

fitting.value: Likelihoods as given in Eqs 2-5; reports medians and 68% credible intervals

evidence.quote: We provide the median values of our MCMC chains and report 68 percent credible intervals throughout.

validation.value: Monte Carlo injection of 441 fake sources into residual maps

evidence.quote: We inject a total of 441 fake sources for each case we test below.

analysis_steps.goal: Test temperature evolution with selection effects

method.value: Bootstrap Symeonidis sample, assign ALESS redshifts, apply 3.5 sigma ALMA 870 um limit, compute mean Td for L=1e12-1e13

evidence.quote: We retain those sources that have a predicted flux density greater than the 3.5 $\sigma$ ALMA flux limit at 870 $\mu$m and calculate the mean dust temperature of this sample of sources.

results_numeric.quantity: Mean Td of ALESS sample, full

evidence.quote: For the full sample, we find an average dust temperature of (33.9$\pm$2.4) K.
We find a mean dust temperature of (35.6$\pm$0.8) K.
we find a mean dust temperature of (33.7$\pm$4.2) K for the ALESS sample

results_numeric.quantity: Td offset vs Swinbank et al.

evidence.quote: An apparent systematic shift towards warmer dust temperatures is seen for our results, with an amplitude around 4 K
The standard deviations of the residuals are 1.5, 1.6 and 1.4 mJy at 250 $\mu$m, 350 $\mu$m and 500 $\mu$m, respectively

findings_qualitative.value: Source degeneracies with neighbours dominate parameter uncertainties; a second ALMA band helps most when the SED peak is straddled

evidence.quote: degeneracies between the two sources are nearly eliminated when adding a second ALMA band.
Good agreement is found between our expected uncertainties and the Monte Carlo injected sources.

claims.hypothesis: Average dust temperature evolves with redshift
claims.experiment: Compared ALESS to selection-matched Symeonidis sample

evidence.quote: we cannot conclude that we detect any evolution in dust temperature with redshift in the ALESS sources

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Free beta over 1-2.5 rejected since data lack constraining power

evidence.quote: We found that our data have almost no constraining power on the dust emissivity index, $\beta$

limitations_admitted.value: SED model lacks a hot short-wavelength component and shorter/longer wavelength data

evidence.quote: primarily the lack of a shorter wavelength hot component to our SED model

referee_caveats_inferred: Redshift priors from photometric estimates dominate some results
